description: Run once in a Microsoft Fabric App scaffolded from Rayfin's data app template, before the first chart: installs @bicharts/chart-host (at this server's version) and d3, adds src/lib/bic-chart-options.ts (the app's Fabric theme as chart options) and src/components/bic-chart-panel.tsx (a chart box that measures itself and shows the query's loading, error and empty states) and .agents/skills/regiabi-charts/SKILL.md, ignores .bic/, and puts every @microsoft/rayfin-* package on npm's latest, the release `rayfin init` installs (run it before rayfin init; every package.json range it changes is listed, and the reply names the Rayfin version installed). Never overwrites a file; the one template file it edits - a vi.mock that fixes the template's own validate-visual test under ESM - is named in the reply, as is the one line of src/main.tsx it points at src/lib/bic-css-theme.ts (the theme without bundling Vega). With features: ["notes"] and/or ["scenarios"] (once Rayfin's data service is on), it also adds finished notes-on-marks and saved-scenario files - the Rayfin entities, registered in rayfin/data/schema.ts, a hook each, a notes dialog and a scenarios panel - built on chart-host's useBicFilter / useBicControls; write none of that by hand. Replies with a worked example that renders a generated chart from a live query.

features.description: Also add finished files for readers' notes on chart marks ("notes") and saved settings of a chart's own controls ("scenarios", e.g. a What-if chart's rate). Needs Rayfin's data service on (rayfin/data/schema.ts); the reply says the command when it isn't. Never overwrites.

project_dir.description: The Fabric App project folder. Defaults to the working directory, or the one Fabric App folder directly inside it.

skip_install.description: Add the files only; don't run npm install.

name: setup_fabric_app
title: Set up a Fabric App for these charts
